mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which often precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by > 5% MoM and UNRATE decreases by > 0.2% MoM, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing at a rate of more than 2% YoY, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month signals a strong labor market, which typically supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 jobs per month for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is decreasing and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) is increasing, it indicates a supply-demand mismatch that can lead to inflationary pressures and monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO is decreasing and RSAFS is increasing, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.
